newsitem.title: UK: Rexam reviewing units for possible disposal.
newsitem.headline: Rexam reviewing units for possible disposal.

text.p: Rexam Plc said on Tuesday it was reviewing businesses with sales "in excess of 250 million stg per annum" for possible disposal.
"The impact of this disposal programme will be to improve the return on sales and return on net assets of the group," the packaging and materials group said in a statement.
Rexam said its main objective was to refine its portfolio "so that it is focused on opportunities for profitable growth within each sector".
A disposals programme is already underway "with the objective of tidying up the underperforming tail of each sector", it said.

Rexam said there were a significant number of businesses which "despite strong market positions, do not generate adequate returns. It is the immediate priority of the new management team to develop profit improvement programmes for these busineses".
If any fail to respond, more disposals will be considered.
"The group is now generally well invested. The board expects, therefore, to see capital expenditure running at a lower level than previously over the next few years," Rexam said.
